clue.text: Looks around for possible subscribers

definitions.meaning: searches an area for gold or opportunity, as a miner does
potential customers or clients worth pursuing

explanation.surface: A magazine's sales team scouts about for people who might sign up.
explanation.definitionFit: To prospect is to search or explore; prospects are also likely future customers, two senses of one word.

clue.text: Ornaments for casks

definitions.meaning: decorative tubular trims or piped decorations
a pipe is a large wine barrel

explanation.surface: Decorations meant for barrels.
explanation.definitionFit: Piped decorations adorn cakes and clothes; a pipe is also a large barrel for wine or port.

clue.text: Unfashionable to throw a fit at this enormity

parts.note: out means out of fashion
rage means rant furiously

explanation.surface: Someone dated loses their temper at some atrocity.
explanation.definitionFit: An enormity is a monstrous wrong, an atrocity.

clue.text: Fellow claiming to be chairperson

parts.note: one who professes, ie claims, and who holds a university chair, a senior academic

explanation.surface: A man asserting he chairs the meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'to be a chairperson'.
explanation.definitionFit: A holder of a university chair, and literally one who professes or claims.

clue.text: Lancers left unusually dejected

indicators.note: unusually says the letters are arranged in an unusual way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cavalrymen left behind were strangely downcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Downcast after failure, a synonym of dejected.

clue.text: Sir Edmund Gosse's role in autobiography

definitions.text: Sir Edmund Gosse's role in autobiography

parts.words: Sir Edmund Gosse's role in autobiography
parts.note: Gosse's memoir Father and ... tells of his upbringing; he plays the second part of the title

explanation.surface: A trivia question about a Victorian critic's memoir.
explanation.definitionFit: Gosse's memoir is Father and Son, and he is the boy in it.

clue.text: Form of growth contributing to popular charities

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some kind of development is helped along by well-liked good causes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree is a form of plant growth, and this deciduous conifer is one such tree.

clue.text: Weapon supplied gratuitously to the self-employed?

definitions.text: Weapon supplied gratuitously to the self-employed?

parts.words: Weapon supplied gratuitously to the self-employed?
parts.note: a weapon that is free, put after free, gives a word for a self-employed worker

explanation.surface: Arms handed out for nothing to freelancers.
explanation.walkthrough: Free (gratuitously) plus the weapon makes the word for a self-employed worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spear is a weapon; free plus it describes the self-employed.

clue.text: Race meeting, for instance, held during oil upset

indicators.note: held during says the instance word sits inside the oil word
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: attar is a fragrant oil from roses
eg means for example

explanation.surface: A race day, say, takes place amid an oil spill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oil upset' reads as a spill, but attar is the perfume oil from roses; in a down clue 'upset' turns it upside down, and 'held during' puts EG inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat-racing event is a race meeting.

clue.text: Countryman supervised church bar

parts.note: a hind is a farm labourer
ran means managed
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A rural worker ran a church pub.
explanation.walkthrough: HIND is an old word for a farmhand.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle or impediment is a bar.

clue.text: Depression caused by marijuana? Awkward situation

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis
being in a hole means being in trouble

explanation.surface: Feeling low brought on by cannabis leaves someone in a tricky spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A hollow in a road surface is a dip, a physical depression.

clue.text: Minority almost halved once — to this figure?

indicators.note: almost says the word for minority loses its last letter

parts.note: nonage is the state of being legally under age

indicators.note: halved says only the first half of the word once is used

explanation.surface: A small group nearly split in two once, and the question is what shape results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims NONAGE to NONAG; 'halved' keeps ON, the first half of ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nine-sided polygon is a geometric figure.

clue.text: Fashion pattern

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to form or mould something
an outline or form to follow

explanation.surface: A dressmaker's template, seen as fashion and pattern side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To fashion is to mould into form, and a pattern is an outline or form, both senses of one word.

clue.text: He persecutes people in the hills

indicators.note: in says the word for people is placed within the two hill words

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill on Dartmoor, so two hills give two of them
men means people

explanation.surface: Someone harassing folk out in the hill country.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop in south-west England; MEN goes between two of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who inflicts suffering on others is a persecutor.

clue.text: Purpose of trees in road, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters may form something else

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Why plant trees along a highway?
explanation.definitionFit: The reason for existing, a French phrase meaning purpose.

clue.text: Generation successively distinguished by gold, silver and bronze

definitions.meaning: a period of time or span of people

definitions.text: successively distinguished by gold, silver and bronze
definitions.meaning: the classical ... of mankind were named golden, silver and bronze in turn

explanation.surface: A family line marked in turn by medals, like Olympic placings.
explanation.definitionFit: A generation is a span of time, and Greek myth names successive eras of mankind golden, silver and bronze.

clue.text: An aide is seated so much in Rouen

parts.note: in French assis means seated, signalled by in Rouen
tant is French for so much, signalled by in Rouen

explanation.surface: A helper sits a lot in a Normandy city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Rouen' says both pieces are French words.
explanation.definitionFit: A helper is an aide.

clue.text: National power supply by the Caribbean?

parts.note: a nationality, here that of Spain
the mains supply electricity

explanation.surface: A country's electricity grid running along the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the historical coast is beside the Caribbean, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The old name for the Spanish-held mainland coast of the Caribbean, haunt of pirates.

clue.text: Scholar writing on Henry Ford's bunk

definitions.text: Scholar writing on Henry Ford's bunk

parts.words: Scholar writing on Henry Ford's bunk
parts.note: Henry Ford said history is bunk, so a scholar writing on it studies the past

explanation.surface: An academic scribbling on a car magnate's bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Ford said that history is bunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer on the past is a scholar of history.

clue.text: Useful groups beheaded wrongly — quite unnecessary

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters are set out in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: beheaded removes the first letter of groups

explanation.surface: Helpful teams being decapitated in error was quite pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' turns GROUPS into ROUPS; 'wrongly' shuffles USEFUL plus ROUPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something surplus to need is excessive, exactly what quite unnecessary means.

clue.text: Grazing land beyond the river

parts.note: past means beyond
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Meadows over the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A field for livestock to feed in is grazing land.

clue.text: Sanctimonious-sounding bird

indicators.note: sounding says the word for sanctimonious is heard, not spelt

parts.note: pi is short for pious, self-righteous

explanation.surface: A self-righteous-seeming bird.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is old slang for pious; the bird is the magpie, which Chambers also calls a pie.
explanation.definitionFit: An old name for the magpie, a common black-and-white bird.

clue.text: Bloomer made by prudish university student on April Ist

parts.note: prim means prudish
L, a learner

indicators.note: Ist is the first letter, printed with a capital I

explanation.surface: A gaffe by a prim undergraduate on April Fool's Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake but means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering plant is a bloomer.

clue.text: Endured being taken to court, without stigma

indicators.note: without means outside, so the court word goes around the stigma word

parts.note: sued means taken to law
a stain is a mark of disgrace

explanation.surface: Someone lasted out a lawsuit with no blot on their name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasted through or bore something, a synonym of endured.

clue.text: Rodents found under a church vestment

indicators.note: found under in a down clue places the rodents beneath the letter a

parts.note: mice are rodents

explanation.surface: Mice discovered beneath a priest's robe.
explanation.definitionFit: A white linen cloth worn by a priest is a church vestment.

clue.text: Compound? Neat, I'd say

indicators.note: say tells you to hear the phrase spoken aloud

parts.note: neat is old word for cattle, an ox, followed by I'd

explanation.surface: A drinker ordering a spirit straight, chemistry aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' is an old word for cattle, giving OX; 'Ox, I'd' spoken runs together.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical compound of oxygen with another element.

clue.text: Insulting about Simbel's one day of victory

one is the Roman numeral I
VE Day is Victory in Europe Day

explanation.surface: A rude remark about Simbel on a triumphant day.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks what goes with Simbel: ABU, from Abu Simbel in Egypt, with the 's.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude and offensive speech is abusive.

clue.text: Form of nutrition around Gateshead, say

indicators.note: around says the word for say goes around the gate's head

parts.note: eg, for example
the head of gate is its first letter

explanation.surface: A diet around a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town in north-east England; read as 'gate's head' it gives G.
explanation.definitionFit: A food item eaten for nourishment.

clue.text: Gift for leaders of troops raiding Indonesian island

indicators.note: leaders of picks the first letter of each following word

parts.note: Bute is an island in western Scotland

explanation.surface: A present for commanders of soldiers attacking an island in Indonesia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indonesian' gives only its first letter; the island is Bute, off the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A payment or offering made in homage is a gift.

clue.text: Subject matter of article number one?

parts.note: the is the definite article
number one means oneself, me

explanation.surface: What a leading piece of writing is about.
explanation.definitionFit: The topic of a piece is its subject matter.

clue.text: Flourishing estate in the country

parts.note: green means growing and vigorous
land is property or an estate

explanation.surface: A thriving property out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A large Arctic island and country.
